07/22/2025 07:23 AM EDT Quads/GIP Update: 3Q25 Updated Macro Themes Deck
 
Takeaway: There are several important elements to note in this Macro update.
 
CLICK HERE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/40793505.140/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcHAuaGVkZ2V5ZS5jb20vbXMvaGVfM3EyNV9tYWNyb190aGVtZXM_ZW5jb2RlZF9kYXRhPVR5QVgsN0JoZmsxRXhKUkRENFJaNWZ6U1dRQW1TU2tJPSw/5cbdd6b62ddf9c0a4d20e4e0C5533ac5d> FOR UPDATED 2Q25 THEMES DECK

US REAL ECONOMIC GROWTH:

The advance read for Q2 GDP will be released next Wednesday, 7/30 at 8:30am. The latest refresh of our Nowcast estimate for Q2 Y/Y GDP growth took our estimate lower by -1bp to +1.74%, down from our +1.75% prior estimate. Notably, of the 21 incremental data points since our last update, 14 worsened in RoC terms while 7 improved.  Our refreshed estimate for Q2 Y/Y GDP growth of 1.74% equates to a Q/Q SAAR estimate of +1.98% vs our prior estimate of +2.02%. Bear in mind, the time-shifting distortions manifest in Q2 GDP are still in full effect. April was boosted by pull-forward activity, and May was left in its RoC wake. This is also exactly what our Monthly Quad expectation called for – RoC accel in April followed by decel in May.  Meanwhile, Net Exports and Inventory components of GDP remain heavily impacted by tariff-related dynamics – a conspicuous mathematical headwind to Q1 growth and a mathematical tailwind to Q2.

Our 1.74% Y/Y growth estimate equates to a -25bps RoC decel for Q2 relative to the Q1 actual of 1.99% Y/Y growth. This puts it right around the boundary of shallow decel, aka largely unremarkable. Also notable is that the sequential SAAR growth of 1.98% is clearly non-recessionary.

Looking ahead to Q3 data, thus far we have only the higher-frequency datapoints as none of the July monthly figures are yet available. Looking across weekly initial jobless claims, weekly MBA Mortgage Purchase Applications, and Weekly Rail Traffic, we find that two of the three are improved in RoC terms vs the Q2 rate – claims and mortgage apps – while one – rail traffic – is worse in RoC terms. Bear in mind this is only two weeks of data across three variables and shouldn’t be overly relied upon, but nevertheless it’s useful to know what the early data is suggesting.

On a Nowcast/Forecast Quarterly basis, we continue to expect Quad 3 for Q3 2025, Quad 2 for Q4 2025, and Quad 1 for Q1 2026.

See the slides below for context.

(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/40793505.140/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNDMzMjcvb3JpZ2luYWwvMS5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPXRpbXNtaXRoYXZpYXRpb25AZ21haWwuY29t/5cbdd6b62ddf9c0a4d20e4e0C7bc83eec>)

(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/40793505.140/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNDMzMjcvb3JpZ2luYWwvMy5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPXRpbXNtaXRoYXZpYXRpb25AZ21haWwuY29t/5cbdd6b62ddf9c0a4d20e4e0C19ddec50>)

Monthly Quads:

Our Monthly Quads proxy growth through the lens of consumption, the largest (~70%) component of GDP, and a good overall proxy for economic activity, but can and often do diverge from the Quarterly Quads as they don’t incorporate Government Spending, Investment or Net Exports.

Our outlook for Q2 Monthly Quads is for Quad 2/Quad 3 in the 4 months of August through November. There is a Quad 4 in December, followed by back-to-back Quad 1’s in January and February of 2026 and a Quad 3 in March 2026. We expect April 2026 will be a Quad 1 and May will be a Quad 2. Interestingly, this suggests that four of the five months to start 2026 will be Quad 1 months (Jan, Feb, Apr) or Quad 2 (May), an unambiguously positive start to the new year.

(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/40793505.140/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNDMzMjcvb3JpZ2luYWwvNC5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPXRpbXNtaXRoYXZpYXRpb25AZ21haWwuY29t/5cbdd6b62ddf9c0a4d20e4e0Cac2421b5>)

US Inflation:

2H Inflation:

Our July CPI Nowcast is 2.60% Y/Y, decelerating by -6bps.

After July, our current Forecast framework expects CPI to do the following:

August Accelerate

September Accelerate

October Accelerate

November Accelerate

December Disinflate

January Disinflate

February Disinflate

March Accelerate

April Disinflate

May Accelerate

Next two FOMC Meetings:  July 30th (Hawkish, hotter June CPI, strong labor – 95% probability of no rate cut),  September 17th (Potentially Dovish, 59% of one quarter point cut)

July CPI Release Date:  August 12th

(VIEW LARGER IMAGE <https://model2.hedgeye.com/click/40793505.140/aHR0cHM6Ly9kMXloaWxzNml3aDVsNS5jbG91ZGZyb250Lm5ldC9jaGFydHMvcmVzaXplZC8xNDMzMjcvb3JpZ2luYWwvNS5wbmc_c3JjPWVtYWlsJmVtYWlsPXRpbXNtaXRoYXZpYXRpb25AZ21haWwuY29t/5cbdd6b62ddf9c0a4d20e4e0Caf9bbbca>)

Quarterly Inflation Outlook:

For Q2, Headline CPI averaged 2.45%, down ~30bps from Q1’s 2.74%.

For Q3, we expect Headline CPI to average 2.74% for the quarter, flat from our prior estimate of 2.61%. Interestingly, while we expect inflation to decelerate in July, we expect reacceleration in both August and September.

For Q4, we expect Headline CPI to average 3.06%, up from our prior estimate of 2.94%.

For Q1 2026, we expect Headline CPI to average 2.76%, up slightly from our prior estimate of 2.74%.

Here’s a look at our updated Quarterly CPI projection through Q1 2026. We’ll be rolling out our model for Q2 2026 post the release of Q2 GDP data next week.
